narrative.overview:
Rinzler Portfolio is an Experience-mode surface built around The Gilded Research Instrument. A Soot Black field carries handled evidence objects with Burnished Brass calibrations, dark metal edges, deliberate typography, and personal material details. The interface is tactile, precise, and personal: it feels operated and inspected rather than merely viewed.

Atmosphere stays behind proof. Full-bleed media, quiet texture, pixel details, filigree, paper, and handwriting create presence, while fixed navigation, measured labels, explicit focus, and complete static fallbacks keep the work legible. Components are treated as handled evidence objects: structural at rest, lifted in response, and never detached from their purpose.
keyCharacteristics: Experience mode with artifact-led first viewport composition.
Tactile, precise, personal surfaces built as handled evidence objects.
Burnished Brass calibration on a Soot Black field.
Complete keyboard, reduced-motion, reduced-data, and forced-colors states.

rules.name: The Brass Rarity Rule
rules.body: Burnished Brass is the only global accent; reserve it for focus, selection, evidence, short rules, and small measured inversions.

rules.name: The Material Color Rule
rules.body: Cool Instrument Steel, Project Paper, Note Gold, and Vine Green stay inside the components whose materials they describe; they do not become page themes.

rules.name: The Voice by Function Rule
rules.body: Danviska names, Kiona labels and acts, Recursive explains and measures, Mackie Pixel stamps, and Caveat Note speaks personally.

rules.name: The Pixel Integrity Rule
rules.body: Keep Mackie Pixel on whole-pixel render sizes, pair Mackie Pixel Shine only as its aligned highlight layer, and never smooth its edges with blur.

rules.name: The One Measure Rule
rules.body: Headings and primary instruments share the 72rem measure; only an interaction that needs travel may run wider.

rules.name: The Reflow, Don't Remove Rule
rules.body: Responsive layouts may stack, compress, or scroll, but they preserve every evidence object and its reading order.

rules.name: The Structural at Rest Rule
rules.body: Establish thickness with border, tonal layering, and inset light before using lift; response may deepen the ambient shadow but must preserve the object's material.

rules.name: The Finished Fallback Rule
rules.body: Motion may reveal, turn, drift, or settle an object, but the no-motion state always shows the complete final composition.

rules.name: The Radius by Object Rule
rules.body: Use 4px for controls, 6px for identity and achievement objects, 9px for chapters, and 10px for enclosing windows; do not round every layer alike.

rules.name: The Edge Carries Meaning Rule
rules.body: A border describes construction, selection, or clipping; ornamental edges stay local to the object whose material they explain.

rules.name: The Handled Evidence Rule
rules.body: Interaction should feel like inspecting, turning, selecting, or lifting a specific object; never substitute generic floating containers for the implemented material behavior.

dos: Do keep Burnished Brass scarce and attach it to focus, selection, evidence, or calibrated emphasis.
Do preserve the 72rem measure and let signature objects break it only when their interaction requires room.
Do give every hover or motion behavior an equivalent keyboard state and a complete static fallback.
Do keep photographs, drawings, fonts, and other identity assets credited according to their provenance.
Do treat controls, chapters, stamps, seals, and notes as handled evidence objects with material-specific behavior.
donts: Don't turn component-local steel, paper, note, or vine colors into competing global themes.
Don't replace fixed utilitarian navigation with decorative portfolio chrome.
Don't flatten materially distinct surfaces into one generic container treatment.
Don't import a separate content-world metaphor; keep the visual language grounded in instruments and handled evidence objects.
Don't make ambient video, 3D instruments, pointer tilt, or scroll effects prerequisites for understanding or operation.
